title: Invocation Context Sankey Wires & Grooming
content:
Purpose: capture a different visual approach for per-invocation token cost + latency exploration. Instead of the existing token-slice/trace-first views, this doc proposes a Sankey-style 'Invocation Context' view that connects token groups to cost/latency sinks (model, region, batching, cache). Goal is a quick glance that surfaces dominant cost contributors and fast paths to optimization (caching, model variant, quantization).

Audience: product designers, frontend engineers, infra routing owners, and solutions engineers. This is a working doc for early wireframes and grooming; expect rough diagrams and open questions.

High-level idea: For any selected invocation or time-slice (e.g., 15m, last 100 invocations) show a left-to-right Sankey: leftmost nodes are invocation contexts (route, model version, customer tier), middle nodes are token groupings (prompt prefix, system, user, assistant, tool calls), rightmost nodes are sinks: compute (gpu type + kernel profile), KV/cache hits, batching aggregation, and fallback model tiers. Width represents cost (USD) and color saturation encodes latency contribution (ms). Hover/expand shows token-level list and trace links to Token Inspector.

Design advantages: compact visual summary for non-UX experts; highlights multi-dimensional tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs cache hit rate); natural for comparing two cohorts (A/B) by stacking two Sankeys.

Wireframe hints (desktop):
- Top bar: invocation selector (single invocation id or cohort selector), time range, compare toggle (compare cohort B).
- Left column: invocation metadata card (route, user id hash, pinned model version, pipeline config, trace id link).
- Main canvas: Sankey with three lane groups (context -> token groups -> sinks). Controls: metric toggle (cost | latency | token-count), highlight top N contributors, threshold slider for minor flows.
- Right panel: detailed pane. When clicking a flow, show: token list (with offsets), per-token cost estimate, KV/cache hit indicator, server-side trace snippet (first/last 3 steps), suggested optimization actions.
- Bottom: timeline sparkline of average per-token latency and cost for the selected cohort with brush to update Sankey time window.

Mobile considerations: simplified single-column Sankey condensed to stacked bands; drilldowns via full-screen modal; leave out cohort compare. Focus on critical flows only (top 3 sinks).

Accessibility: ensure color-blind safe palette (Sankey uses pattern overlays on hover), keyboard navigation between flows, ARIA labels for node groups, textual summary export (CSV/JSON) for screen readers.

Interaction flows (detailed):
1) Open invocation -> Sankey populates -> hover a sink -> small tooltip with cost delta vs baseline -> click sink -> right panel opens with recommended mitigations (e.g., enable KV cache with sample prompt segments).
2) Compare mode: choose second cohort -> two Sankeys stacked horizontally with diff mode (green/red ribbons) -> click diff to focus on invocations that materially drove the delta -> open Token Inspector for one sample invocation.
3) From right panel -> 'Create runbook' action pre-fills steps (check cache, test quantized variant, route to cheaper region) and links to deployment playbook template.

Suggested visual encodings:
- Flow width: dollar-per-invocation normalized to cohort size.
- Color saturation: average latency contribution split by token group.
- Dashed outline: flows that involve fallbacks or degraded quality models.
- Iconography: small chip for GPU type, stack icon for batching, lightning bolt for cold starts.

Data model / sample fields required from backend:
- invocation_id, route, model_version, region, tier, sequence_length, token_spans (grouped by role), per_token_cost_usd, per_token_latency_ms, kv_hit_boolean, batch_id, backend_node_type, fallback_flag.

Sample table row (for reference):
- "invocation_12345 | route: /chat | model: redwood-3B-q4 | region: us-west1 | tokens: 212 | total_cost_usd: 0.0042 | avg_latency_ms: 310 | kv_hits: 62% | batch: batch-432"

Backend considerations and API endpoints (mock):
- GET /api/analytics/invocations?cohort=last_100&metric=cost -> returns aggregated flows compatible with Sankey layout.
- GET /api/analytics/invocation/{id}/tokens -> returns token list with per-token metrics and cache flags.
- POST /api/diagnostics/runbook -> creates templated mitigation playbook (links to ticket).

Grooming backlog (candidate tickets):
- PLAT-5489: Sankey layout engine integration (data-to-edges mapping)
- PLAT-5490: Cohort compare mode (delta rendering)
- PLAT-5491: Right-panel recommendations engine (simple rule-based first)
- PLAT-5492: Token list API + pagination for large invocations
- PLAT-5493: Accessibility pass + automated color-blind palette tests

Each backlog item below includes acceptance criteria and a rough estimate.

Backlog item details:
- "PLAT-5489 - Sankey layout engine integration":
  Acceptance criteria: Sankey renders for single-cohort with accurate flow widths (within 2% of computed cost), hover shows tooltip with numeric cost and latency breakdown, supports top-N thresholding.
  Estimate: "5" story points

- "PLAT-5490 - Cohort compare mode":
  Acceptance criteria: Two cohorts can be selected, diff overlay shows increases/decreases, clicking a diff ribbon filters invocation list to those contributing >10% delta.
  Estimate: "3" story points

- "PLAT-5491 - Right-panel recommendations engine":
  Acceptance criteria: For a clicked sink, the engine returns at least 2 actionable suggestions (cache, model variant, reroute), with links to runbook creation; suggestions should be deterministic for same input.
  Estimate: "3" story points

- "PLAT-5492 - Token list API":
  Acceptance criteria: Tokens can be streamed/paginated, per-token cost and latency values included, API responds within 200ms for first page for a 200-token invocation.
  Estimate: "2" story points

- "PLAT-5493 - Accessibility pass":
  Acceptance criteria: Color contrast ratios meet WCAG AA for primary flows, keyboard-only navigation covers 90% interactions, voiceover textual summary available.
  Estimate: "1" story point

Open questions / risks: 
- How do we map 'cost per token' when tokenization differs across models? Need a canonical tokenizer or to show model-specific token counts.
- Privacy: invocation_id needs redaction when shared externally. Right-panel must only show hashed user ids.
- Cohort selection UX: power users want query-level filters (route, model, region) while product managers prefer time-range + top-N. Need both.
- Performance: generating Sankey for a 15m high-traffic window may be expensive. Consider pre-aggregations and sampling heuristics.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Sync with infra/team owning routing to confirm availability of per-token cost signals (Jonah).
2) Prototype static SVG Sankey with sample aggregated dataset (design spike: 2 days).
3) Run a lightning user test (5 participants: SEs + SREs) to validate concept clarity and whether Sankey surfaces actionability vs existing token-inspector.
4) Groom backlog items and split PLAT-5489 into frontend/backend subtasks in next refinement.

Notes-to-self: save a copy of the prototype datasets (anonymized) in the analytics bucket, include one 'weird' outlier invocation to validate dashed fallback flows.

Attachments/Sketch ideas (to convert into proper wireframes):
- Sketch A: single-cohort sankey with three lane groups (hand-drawn boxes).
- Sketch B: stacked cohort compare with diff ribbons.
- Sketch C: mobile condensed band + drilldown modal.

End of doc.
wireframe_notes: Use left metadata card to show immediate remediation actions (e.g., toggle cache)
Edge grouping: collapse flows under 0.5% cost into 'other' to reduce visual noise
Hover micro-interactions: small chip indicating percent of total cost and sample token snippet
Comparison mode should allow locking one cohort to keep baseline fixed
interaction_flows: Open invocation -> Sankey populates -> hover sink -> tooltip with cost and latency -> click -> open right panel with actionable mitigations
Enable compare -> pick cohort B -> two sankeys render -> diff ribbons show increases/decreases -> drill into most changed flows
From right panel -> create runbook -> auto-fill with suggested steps and create ticket in JIRA
acceptance_criteria: Sankey width reflects cost USD within 2% for single cohort
Clicking flow shows token-level detail in right panel
Compare mode shows diff ribbons and filters invocation list by delta
API returns first page of tokens for 200-token invocation within 200ms
